blocks.h: What a preventive maintenance visit covers
blocks.intro: Written from your design and qualification records, agreed before the first visit.

items.d: Conductivity, total organic carbon (TOC), temperature, flow and alarm history since the last visit, so the work answers the trend.
Reverse osmosis (RO) and electrodeionization (EDI): normalized flow, salt passage and differential pressure to ASTM D4516 against the commissioning baseline.
Seals, gaskets and diaphragms replaced like for like, lot numbers recorded; vent filters integrity tested.
Return flow against the qualified minimum, pump and heat exchanger condition, point-of-use valves.
Softener hardness leakage, carbon bed or bisulfite performance, total chlorine at the RO inlet.
Lamp intensity, ozone below the release limit, sanitization checked at its coldest or weakest point.

blocks.h: Questions maintenance, validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Will service work affect our qualified state?
items.a: Not when it is maintenance done like for like under your procedure: same part, same specification, return-to-service checks, record filed. Anything else stops, and we give you the input for your change request, including the IQ, OQ or sampling we propose. See commissioning and qualification for how requalification scope is set.

items.q: Can your technicians work to our SOPs and forms?
items.a: Yes. We complete your work orders, logbooks or calibration forms as well as or instead of ours, and follow your standard operating procedures (SOPs). Scope, method statement and training records arrive [visit scope lead time, working days] ahead; technicians take your site induction and follow your gowning rules.

items.q: How do severities and the response clock work?
items.a: Severity 1: production stopped or water out of specification at a point of use. Severity 2: running with an alarm, reduced capacity or a trend toward an alert level. Severity 3: no effect on quality or supply. Severity 4: planned work. The clock starts when you log the request by phone or form and stops when [response clock stop event].

items.q: What happens if you miss a response time?
items.a: [missed response remedy]. Each severity 1 response is recorded with the time logged and the time on site, and the annual review shows our record for your system. Response times apply inside [service coverage area]; outside it, we agree a travel response time in the plan schedule before you sign.

items.q: Do you service systems built by another manufacturer?
items.a: Yes, for [makes and equipment types serviced]. No Aquemi serial number is needed: log a service request with the make and model. We start with a condition survey and a review of drawings, qualification records and spares, because a like-for-like replacement needs a known original.

items.q: We have our own maintenance team. Why a plan?
items.a: Many sites keep routine work in-house and buy what needs specialist tools or references: USP <645> and <643> calibrations, RO and EDI diagnostics, vent filter integrity tests, the annual review and fast response on a critical fault. The tier 1 plan is written for that split.

items.q: Which spares should we hold, and are they proprietary?
items.a: Your ranked spares list comes with the turnover package, each line with manufacturer, model and certificates. On site, we recommend loop pump seals, conductivity and TOC spares, UV lamps, diaphragms per valve size and a vent filter. Parts are standard where the design allows. Plan stock is held at [spares stock locations], shipped [order cut-off and delivery commitment].

items.q: What does a service plan cost?
items.a: It depends on the system, its age, the number of instruments and your distance from [nearest service base]. Plans start at [lowest plan price, CAD per year]. Send the details below and we return a fixed annual price and the first-visit scope.
